nodes.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: C-|h_t|<T_comp=10240 tokens (equals max assistant response); at most 3 compactions; resume = system + u_resume(S_t) + last k=2 raw steps
nodes.notes: Main recipe prefers summary tokens: 'summary tokens are sampled from the same trainable policy and are included in the RL objective' and 'All execution and summary segments are optimized and share the trajectory reward R'. The w/o-summary-training ablation 'enables compaction during training but masks out the loss on summary-response turns'; Table 3 'Summary Train indicates whether summary responses are included in the RL loss'. Exposure-only (masked summaries) still lifts compacted SWE-Verified 50.5→54.5 (30B) and 59.8→64.5 (106B); adding summary training reaches 56.0/66.8. GLM-4.5-Air-SFT is ordinary SFT on GLM-4.7 trajectories (PDF does not say those SFT trajs contain compaction).

nodes.title: ACM: Agentic Context Management for Long Horizon Tasks
nodes.trigger_detail: agent-initiated manage_context + query_memory; teacher injects/removes calls; student resumes from teacher-edited action
nodes.notes: On-policy distillation loss is over all assistant tokens: 'The student is optimized to match these teacher distributions over all assistant-token positions in the rollout' and 'The loss is applied to all student-generated assistant tokens, while system-prompt, user-input, and tool-output tokens are masked out.' manage_context/query_memory calls (when to compact) are therefore preferred targets. The actual summary text is produced by a summarizer LLM as a tool result, so it is tool-output and masked. Resume-from-edit: 'the student's original action a_t is replaced with the teacher-annotated action a_t' and the student rollout resumes from a_t'. Rejection sampling keeps only trajectories where the student fails all trials; mix with resampled student rollouts.

nodes.title: Context as a Tool: Context Management for Long-Horizon SWE-Agents (CaT / SWE-Compressor)
nodes.trigger_detail: offline injection of context-management tool calls at hindsight condenser points (subtask / strategy switch / error-correction); summary is the tool Observation
nodes.notes: CaT-Generator injects a context-management Action whose Observation is a teacher-written long-term memory block M(a_i). SFT is on the stitched trajectory (CaT-Instruct, 20k) plus 20k Base-Instruct without context-mgmt. Rejection sampling drops failed trajs and 'unreasonable context-management behaviors'. The paper claims the model learns 'when to compress context, how to generate effective summaries, and how to reuse compressed representations' but never states whether Observation/summary tokens enter the CE loss. Under the stated Action/Observation split, the when-to-call tokens are SFT targets and the summary text is an observation; loss on summary tokens is unknown.

nodes.title: AgentFold: Long-Horizon Web Agents with Proactive Context Management
nodes.trigger_detail: every step emits a folding directive (granular condensation or deep consolidation) plus a tool call; latest interaction kept raw
nodes.notes: Fold-Generator produces pairs {(C_t, R_t*)} where R_t* is the full structured assistant response (thinking, folding directive, explanation, tool call). 'This curated dataset is then used for conducting conventional Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)' whose objective is 'to produce the entire structured output intrinsically'. Folding/summary text is therefore an assistant target (preferred). Rejection sampling discards format-invalid steps and trajs with too many env errors. PDF does not mention loss-masking the folding span.

nodes.title: Scaling Long-Horizon LLM Agent via Context-Folding (FoldGRPO)
nodes.trigger_detail: branch(description, prompt) then return(message); intermediate branch steps folded out of working context
nodes.notes: return(message) is a policy action that writes the branch summary. FoldGRPO 'jointly optimizes the entire interaction trajectory including the main thread and those sub-task branches'. '1_LLM ensures that only those LLM generated tokens are optimized and the tokens from tool observations are masked.' So the summary lives in the return-call tokens (preferred); folded raw branch steps are removed from context, not merely loss-masked. No SFT stage is described. 32K active budget, max 10 branches; SWE-Verified 58.0 vs 55.2 ReAct at 327K.

nodes.title: Scaling LLM Multi-turn RL with End-to-end Summarization-based Context Management (SUPO)
nodes.trigger_detail: periodic summarization when context is overlong (|s|≥L); working context reset to prompt + last summary + post-summary tail
nodes.notes: 'the summary is neither pre-defined nor rule-based, but rather generated by the agent and optimized jointly as part of the agent's policy'. Theorem 3.2 decomposes the policy gradient into tool-use tokens plus 'optimizing summary of current traj.' Overlong masking is not summary-masking: it zeros gradients on rollouts that never emit a final answer before step/summary caps. No SFT recipe. PDF does not describe an SFT-only continuation loss.

nodes.title: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
nodes.trigger_detail: systematic (not agent-initiated) summary-tool trigger; history reset to q'=(q,s)
nodes.notes: Two models. ReSumTool-30B is SFT on 9k+ <Conversation, Summary> pairs — summary tokens preferred for the summarizer. The policy is adapted with ReSum-GRPO, not SFT ('Unlike supervised fine-tuning, which risks overwriting general capabilities'). Segments start from q'=(q,s) so the summary is kept as context; 'all observations o are masked during loss computation as they are environmental returns'. Policy is trained to continue from compacted observations, not to emit the summary. Authors explicitly prefer RL over collecting expert ReSum SFT trajs.

nodes.title: Acon: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: selective history/observation compression when needed; compressor is a separate LLM, not the policy
nodes.notes: Policy weights are not updated on compressed trajectories. Compressor student is trained with token-level CE on teacher summaries: 'We train the student with a cross-entropy objective with input-output pair (x,y)' where y is the compressed history/observation, on tasks where the teacher succeeds with compression. Summary tokens are preferred for the compressor only. Agent continues from compressed context at inference with no special policy loss.

nodes.title: Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; OpenHands CodeAct append-only trajectories
nodes.notes: Filtered behavior cloning, not compaction-aware: 'rejection sampling fine-tuning (a.k.a. filtered behavior cloning), where we fine-tune the base LM on success trajectories sampled from SWE-Gym' — 491 successful teacher trajs (~19 turns, ~19k tokens). Failed trajs discarded. Per-instance cap later because training on all successes biases to easy tasks. PDF never mentions summary tokens or loss-masking compacted spans. OpenHands-LM-32B (37% SWE-Verified in follow-on cards) is this SFT lineage.

nodes.title: SWE-smith: Scaling Data for Software Engineering Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; SWE-agent teacher rollouts on synthetic bugs
nodes.notes: 'we fine-tune the base (or “student”) model on the trajectories corresponding to resolved instances' (RFT). 5,016 expert trajs from 20k Claude 3.7 runs; further cap ≤3 trajs per instance because 'easier' repeated successes degrade performance. Unresolved runs (~61% in later re-analyses of the public traj dump) are discarded, not rewritten. No compacted/summary-token loss rule.

nodes.title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: scaffold supports threshold-compression (CaT's OpenHands baseline); paper itself is the agent platform, not an SFT recipe
nodes.notes: Cited by CaT as the inference scaffold and as the Threshold-Compression baseline (compress when length exceeds a threshold; keep system+intent+last k, summarize the rest). OpenHands-LM SFT follows SWE-Gym success-only cloning. This PDF does not state whether compressor/summary tokens enter student loss.

nodes.title: Agent-FLAN: Designing Data and Methods of Effective Agent Tuning for Large Language Models
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; rewrites ReAct/JSON trajectories into multi-turn chat
nodes.notes: Rewrites, does not compact: 'we first replace the classical Thought-Action-ActionInput templates with multi-turn dialogues' and 'loss will be only applied to the assistant clause'. Capability-decomposed balancing + negative samples for hallucination. No summary-token rule. Closest industry-like default: assistant-only CE after format rewrite.

nodes.title: AgentOhana: Design Unified Data and Training Pipeline for Effective Agent Learning
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; unify heterogeneous trajs then AgentRater-filter
nodes.notes: Quality filter, not compaction filter: AgentRater scores whole trajs 0–5; keep score>=4 (167,918 sampled → 42,600 kept). Explicitly notes env reward can be high while intermediate actions are invalid. No mention of summary/compaction tokens in the loss.

nodes.title: FireAct: Toward Language Agent Fine-tuning
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; GPT-4 ReAct/CoT/Reflexion trajs unified to ReAct
nodes.notes: Fine-tune on 500 GPT-4 agent trajectories (and mixes of ReAct+CoT). Project page: 'These effective paths are then translated into the ReAct format' — keep successful/effective paths, rewrite format. No compacted-span loss rule.

nodes.title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; AgentInstruct = generate, interact, filter
nodes.notes: 1,866 trajs after 'trajectory filter'; GitHub: 'Ours are rigorously filtered using strict rewards to ensure top-notch quality.' Hybrid mix with general instructions. No compaction/summary loss statement.

nodes.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; two-stage SFT selection on resolved SWE trajs
nodes.notes: Closest SWE-SFT analogue of span masking, but for process-quality segments not summaries: 'During SFT, all segments remain in the sequence to preserve context, while only selected segments contribute to the loss computation.' Stage 1 keeps a 10% high-quality subset of successful trajs; stage 2 loss-masks low-contribution/risky segments. Cites SWE-Gym/SWE-smith as success-only SFT. Not a compaction paper.

nodes.title: From Patches to Trajectories: Privileged Process Supervision for Software-Engineering Agents (P2T)
nodes.trigger_detail: no compaction; privileged p* used to curate/shorten SWE-Gym trajs
nodes.notes: Compares outcome-filtered SFT to 'its tool-error-masking variant': error/tool-failure steps can be loss-masked while kept as context. Uses 1.8k curated SWE-Gym instances. Again not about summary tokens; shows SWE SFT already experiments with span masks, but on errors not compactions.

nodes.title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
nodes.trigger_detail: each turn overwrites a constant-size internal memory; raw history not retained at generation time
nodes.notes: Cited by SUPO/ACM/AgentFold as end-to-end memory RL. SUPO's description (not independently re-verified in the MEM1 PDF here): during RL 'the entire history (including all the queries, observations, and internal state representations) are concatenated to a single trajectory to perform policy optimization, where the actual context dependency are encoded in an attention mask.' That is an attention mask, not a documented summary-token loss mask. No SFT recipe extracted.

gaps: No standalone paper does harness-controlled compaction + SFT-only continuation (survey §3.5). Closest SFT papers (CaT, AgentFold, ACM) bundle when+what+continue into an agent tool; closest harness-controlled papers (CompactionRL, SUPO, ReSum-GRPO) are RL.
CaT, SWE-Gym, SWE-smith, FireAct, AgentTuning, AgentOhana, and OpenHands-LM never state whether summary/observation tokens enter CE. Do not invent assistant-only masking for those PDFs.
CompactionRL's GLM-4.5-Air-SFT stage is ordinary SFT on GLM-4.7 trajectories; the PDF does not say those SFT traces contain compaction events.

OpenHands-SFT is a model-card/SWE-Gym lineage, not a paper with a compaction loss recipe. Threshold-compression in CaT's OpenHands baseline is inference-only on a Base-Instruct (no context-mgmt) SFT model.
Industry default (LlamaFactory/Axolotl/Unsloth assistant-only next-token loss, no compaction filter) is not measured in these academic PDFs; contrast is by recipe, not by a head-to-head number.

when: CompactionRL fires at a fixed reserve T_comp=10240 tokens, atomic (a_i,o_i) steps, last-k=2 tail, ≤3 compactions (arxiv:2607.05378).

ACM/CaT/AgentFold/Context-Folding treat compact/fold as an agent-initiated tool at semantic or self-monitored points; ReSum/SUPO use systematic/overlong triggers (arxiv:2607.23809, arxiv:2512.22087, arxiv:2509.13313).
sft: Academic compaction papers do not share one SFT loss. CompactionRL (RL) prefers summary tokens in the objective and only masks them in the w/o-summary-training ablation, which still gets most of the compacted-inference gain (arxiv:2607.05378).

When the summary is a policy action (AgentFold folding directive; Context-Folding return(message); SUPO LLM summary), those tokens are preferred / jointly optimized (arxiv:2510.24699, arxiv:2510.11967, arxiv:2510.06727).

When the summary is a tool Observation or new user prompt, academic recipes train the policy to continue from it and mask tool-outputs: ACM assistant-only distill with tool-output mask; ReSum-GRPO keeps s in q' and masks observations; ACON SFT is compressor-only CE and does not train the policy on summaries (arxiv:2607.23809, arxiv:2509.13313, arxiv:2510.00615).

CaT is the main SFT+offline-injection recipe: inject context-mgmt Actions, put teacher summaries in Observations, rejection-sample successes. The PDF never says whether summary Observation tokens are in the loss — mark unknown/mixed, not assistant-only by invention (arxiv:2512.22087).

SWE-Gym / SWE-smith / OpenHands-LM / FireAct / AgentTuning / AgentOhana filter or rewrite whole trajectories (success-only RFT, reward/AgentRater filters, ReAct↔chat rewrite). They discard failed or low-score trajs; they do not mention compacted spans. SWE-Prime and P2T later loss-mask low-quality or tool-error segments while keeping them as context — still not summary tokens (arxiv:2412.21139, arxiv:2504.21798, arxiv:2608.27449, arxiv:2605.21996).

Versus the expected industry default (LlamaFactory-style assistant-only next-token loss, no special compaction filter): academics either (i) up-weight/include summary tokens when the policy is the summarizer, (ii) mask them when a separate summarizer writes a tool/user span, or (iii) ignore compaction entirely and only success-filter raw ReAct traces. None publish an SFT corpus that discards compacted turns after they have been injected.
